effects.name: Grassroots Expansion
effects.text: Rally may place its Support in a neighboring district instead of its source district.

effects.name: Fresh Start
effects.text: When Organise or Rally restores a party absent from the map, place two Support instead of one, together or separately. Place both if possible; otherwise place one.

effects.name: Carpooling
effects.text: Organise may move two Support together from the same source to the same destination.

effects.name: Established Networks
effects.text: Organise may move between any two districts already containing acting-party Support, regardless of distance.

effects.name: Political Exchange
effects.text: Organise may swap moving Support with rival Support at the destination. Each arrival needs a free spot or a rival to swap back to the source.

effects.name: Long-Reach Campaigns
effects.text: Smear may target a district up to two adjacency steps from acting-party Support.

effects.name: Displacement
effects.text: Instead of removing its target, Smear may move that Support to a free spot in a neighboring district.

effects.name: Cross-Region Campaigns
effects.text: After Organise moves Support across a region boundary, add one acting-party Support in the source district.

effects.name: Muted Priorities
effects.text: At final scoring, each firm treats its printed 6-point issue as worth 4 for both gains and losses. Party votes do not change.

effects.name: Broad Interests
effects.text: At final scoring, each firm treats its printed 1-point issue as worth 3 for both gains and losses. Party votes do not change.

effects.name: New Constituencies
effects.text: Rally may place its Support anywhere in its source region, provided the destination has no acting-party Support.

effects.name: Chain Migration
effects.text: After Organise moves Support, move a different acting-party Support from a neighboring district into a spot vacated in the source district.

effects.name: Bridge Campaign
effects.text: After Organise moves Support across a region boundary, add one acting-party Support at its destination.

effects.name: Regional Express
effects.text: Organise may move to any district in its source region, regardless of distance.

effects.name: Crowded Airwaves
effects.text: Smear may target any full district, regardless of acting-party presence or distance.

policies.name: Mobile Clinics
policies.frontFlavour: The outer burrows have waited eleven years for a clinic. The Council offers them six converted buses and a promise to keep the engines running.
policies.backFlavour: Mrs Brindle’s knees were seen to on Tuesday. Getting to the shops now takes her most of Wednesday.

policies.name: Transport Hubs
policies.frontFlavour: At Millbank, changing buses requires a long walk and considerable faith. A proper interchange is ready to build. So is the clinic extension.
policies.backFlavour: The interchange has a roof, clear signs, and somewhere to sit. Patients waiting outside the clinic have asked for the same.

policies.name: Hospital Accountability
policies.frontFlavour: The hospital insists every complaint is investigated. The families meeting above the bakery would like to know by whom. School inspectors may soon have a new assignment.
policies.backFlavour: For the first time, the hospital published its waiting times. The Gazette printed them beside last year’s promises.

policies.name: Common Curriculum
policies.frontFlavour: At North Bellwether School, the atlas still shows the old border. The headteacher wants new books before another generation learns it incorrectly. The hospital has also submitted a list.
policies.backFlavour: Every classroom received the same new atlas. The hospital’s replacement equipment remains on a map of future improvements.

policies.name: Community Care Routes
policies.frontFlavour: The new estates have show homes, sales offices, and nowhere to dress a wound. Reserve a few ground-floor flats for neighbourhood nurses.
policies.backFlavour: The nurse knows every stairwell on the estate. The housing office would still like its six flats back.

policies.name: New Estate Outreach
policies.frontFlavour: Families keep arriving at the estate office with keys that fit nothing. A permanent housing adviser could help—if the community health team can spare the office and salary.
policies.backFlavour: By winter, every family had a working key and someone to call about the damp. The visiting nurse now comes once a month.

policies.name: Universal Care Charter
policies.frontFlavour: Mrs Brindle brought her rejected claim to the Council and read it aloud. The proposed care guarantee has fifty signatures. The river restoration fund has the money.
policies.backFlavour: The clinic stopped asking whether patients could afford treatment. Downstream, the river wardens were told to make their remaining grant last.

policies.name: Clean Air Relocation
policies.frontFlavour: Laundry on Cinder Lane comes in greyer than it went out. Residents want the municipal incinerator moved. The proposed hospital wing can wait, they say; their lungs cannot.
policies.backFlavour: For the first time in years, Cinder Lane hung out white sheets. The hospital architect put the wing’s drawings back in their tube.

policies.name: Emergency Recruitment
policies.frontFlavour: The night ward has one nurse, two kettles, and a vacancy notice faded almost white. The hospital wants permission to offer wages someone might accept.
policies.backFlavour: Four new nurses arrived before winter. On their first night, the old kettle finally had time to go cold.

policies.name: Spending Restraint
policies.frontFlavour: The Treasurer has circled the hospital wage bill in red. The matron has returned it with the unfilled shifts circled in blue.
policies.backFlavour: The accounts balanced. The matron pinned another blank rota to the staffroom door and began making calls.

policies.name: Shared Commuting
policies.frontFlavour: School coaches sit idle while the early shift walks to Millbank. The Council proposes a shared service; the headteacher has asked to see the timetable.
policies.backFlavour: Workers reached the gates before the whistle. School breakfast now begins twenty minutes earlier.

policies.name: Public Broadcasting
policies.frontFlavour: Bellwether Radio wants to teach evening classes to every kitchen in town. The money would come from the cheap-fare scheme that gets people to the college.
policies.backFlavour: Algebra reached the outer burrows at seven each evening. The last discounted bus to the college disappeared from the timetable.

policies.name: Bridge Construction
policies.frontFlavour: A direct crossing. A shorter commute. A brighter future. Lantern Row does not appear in the artist’s impression.
policies.backFlavour: The opening ceremony lasted an hour. Former residents of Lantern Row watched from the far bank.

policies.name: Neighbourhood Connections
policies.frontFlavour: The bypass plan leaves two halves of a neighbourhood facing a cutting. Residents have submitted another drawing: homes, a courtyard, and the old street joined up again.
policies.backFlavour: Children can walk to their grandparents without crossing the ring road. Through-traffic is still looking for a shortcut.

policies.name: Regional Corridors
policies.frontFlavour: Millbank’s carriers lose half a day on the winding northern road. Their proposed express route is beautifully straight on paper, right through the alder woods.
policies.backFlavour: Deliveries arrived before noon. That spring, residents along the new road began putting up signs for wandering wildlife.

policies.name: Walkable Communities
policies.frontFlavour: The market square has room for forty parked cars or a hundred things worth visiting. The traders agree on that much. They disagree about which brings customers.
policies.backFlavour: The first saplings went in on Monday. By Saturday, someone had put a table beneath each one.

policies.name: Public Bridge Fund
policies.frontFlavour: Three mayors have promised to repair Bellwether’s crossings. This one has brought a borrowing agreement and a photograph of the missing planks.
policies.backFlavour: The weight restrictions came down. The repayments will outlast the mayor’s portrait in the council chamber.

policies.name: Existing Infrastructure
policies.frontFlavour: The Treasurer proposes mending what Bellwether owns before building anything new. Residents beyond the last bus stop have noted the distinction.
policies.backFlavour: The old station roof no longer leaks. Beyond the terminus, the faded sign still promises a future extension.

policies.name: Lifelong Learning
policies.frontFlavour: There are lights on in the vacant flats above the market: someone has started teaching bookkeeping. The college wants to make it official. The housing office wants the keys.
policies.backFlavour: Evening classes filled every room. On the housing register, the same addresses were crossed out in pencil.

policies.name: Housing Exchange
policies.frontFlavour: The old school has fewer pupils each year and more roof than it can afford. A proposal would move the children across town and turn the classrooms into homes.
policies.backFlavour: Twelve households moved in before winter. The former headteacher helped one family hang curtains where the blackboard had been.

policies.name: Distance Learning
policies.frontFlavour: Beyond the ridge, a college place means leaving home. A new teaching network could bring lectures into every burrow, provided the hillside makes room for its humming machinery.
policies.backFlavour: The first graduates collected their certificates without moving away. Above their homes, the server hall glowed through the night.

policies.name: Community Gardens
policies.frontFlavour: After twenty years behind a “School Extension Coming Soon” sign, the vacant lot has acquired beans, beehives, and a fiercely organised gardening committee.
policies.backFlavour: The gardeners won their lease. The headteacher accepted a basket of tomatoes without withdrawing her objection.

policies.name: New Campus Outreach
policies.frontFlavour: The outer districts send their brightest students away and rarely get them back. A local campus has enthusiastic support and a building estimate nobody will read aloud.
policies.backFlavour: The campus opened with borrowed furniture and a full first-year class. For once, the graduation photographs might be taken close to home.

policies.name: Public Spending Scrutiny
policies.frontFlavour: The auditors want every college course to justify its cost. The pottery tutor has invited them to explain “measurable public benefit” to her Wednesday class.
policies.backFlavour: The college met its savings target. The Wednesday class began meeting above the bakery, bringing its own clay.

policies.name: Moving Chains
policies.frontFlavour: Mrs Brindle would gladly leave her draughty house for a smaller one. Build beyond the meadow, says the developer, and half the housing queue could move along behind her.
policies.backFlavour: Mrs Brindle moved into a warm little bungalow. Three households moved in her wake. From her new window, she watches the last strip of meadow.

policies.name: Shared Travel Scheme
policies.frontFlavour: A shared vehicle depot could serve the whole estate. Its proposed site is currently labelled “future homes”; the planners say fewer cars will eventually mean more space.
policies.backFlavour: The estate’s second cars began disappearing. The promised homes beside the depot remained a dotted outline on the plan.

policies.name: Connected Neighbourhoods
policies.frontFlavour: The developer delivered the houses and disappeared before the drains. Residents want the Council to finish the neighbourhood they were sold.
policies.backFlavour: The streetlights came on in November. Residents stood at their windows to watch; the Council began arguing over the bill.

policies.name: Property Exchange
policies.frontFlavour: The Treasurer calls the riverside flats an underperforming asset. The tenants’ association has submitted a list of everyone who lives in it.
policies.backFlavour: The sale cleared a substantial debt. The tenants’ association spent the following month helping its members find somewhere else to live.

policies.name: Green Corridors
policies.frontFlavour: The last two alder woods are separated by fences, sheds, and a strip of land whose owner has suddenly discovered its value. The wardens want to buy a way through.
policies.backFlavour: By spring, the first tracks crossed the restored strip. The purchase price was still being debated in the Gazette.

policies.name: Managed Relocation
policies.frontFlavour: Selling the central works yard would clear a year’s deficit. Its replacement would stand beyond the town boundary, on land the survey calls scrub and the wardens call home.
policies.backFlavour: The old yard fetched more than expected. At the new one, workers regularly stop the machinery to let displaced wildlife pass.
